historical_reviews.deepseek: YES; extracts the displayed enabled count without raw legacy/extended fields, per-socket identity or BIOS-disable semantics.

original_test_intent: Verify the Type 4 number of enabled physical cores for each populated processor, including the extended Enabled Core Count 2 encoding when applicable, matches approved firmware core-disable policy and persists after reboot.
original_method: Capture complete raw/decoded Type 4 records, calculate effective Enabled Core Count from the legacy selector and extended field, bind by socket/status, compare with total Core Count and the approved BIOS/fuse configuration, optionally correlate read-only OS topology, reboot and repeat.
manual_activity: A user approves enabled-core expectations, BIOS/fuse policy, extended-field interpretation, optional OS correlation and reboot plan. Read-only verification is automatable.
required_inputs: Expected enabled physical cores per populated socket
Applicable SMBIOS version and legacy versus Enabled Core Count 2 selection rule
Total Core Count plus approved BIOS core-disable/fused-core configuration
Rule distinguishing firmware-disabled cores from OS-offline logical CPUs
Validated SMBIOS/OS topology tools and approved reboot/OOB recovery plan
safety_requirements: Use read-only SMBIOS/OS queries; do not enable/disable cores, online/offline CPUs, alter SMT or modify BIOS/firmware.
Preserve raw legacy and extended enabled-count fields and formatted length to detect invalid sentinel use.
Require Enabled Core Count not to exceed effective total Core Count, subject only to an explicit applicable specification rule.
Do not infer firmware-disabled cores solely from OS offline state; OS hotplug and visibility are separate layers.
Stop on invalid field combinations, impossible counts, mapping ambiguity, unexpected drift or reboot failure; no automatic retry.
agent_execution_scope: Resolve effective enabled physical-core count per Type 4 record, apply total-count consistency and approved BIOS/fuse/OS correlation before and after reboot.
Do not change core state, normalize an impossible value away or decide PASS/FAIL.
engineer_actions: Approve enabled-core and core-disable/fuse policy plus any OS visibility correlation.
Approve reboot/recovery and issue the formal verdict.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The exact label reduces one ambiguity, but grep still loses socket/raw selector/extended fields and cannot validate Enabled Core Count against total cores or BIOS policy.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Capture full raw/decoded Type 4 data, derive the effective enabled count from legacy/extended fields, bind sockets and validate total-versus-enabled consistency plus approved configuration.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The Enabled Core Count scope, Type 4 script and 10/10-minute values are retained.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Decode Enabled Core Count and Enabled Core Count 2 with formatted-length/version checks, compare each effective value with total Core Count and the approved BIOS/fuse policy, and use OS topology only as layer-aware supporting evidence.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: SMBIOS Type 4 systems, including high-core-count processors requiring extended fields.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record SMBIOS, BIOS settings, CPU SKU/fuse state, parser/dmidecode and OS versions.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Applicable SMBIOS Type 4 Enabled Core Count and Enabled Core Count 2 semantics, approved BIOS/CPU topology policy and installed tool documentation.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds extended encoding, total-versus-enabled consistency and explicit firmware-versus-OS state separation.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: No reduction; finds truncation, impossible counts and policy mismatches that a label grep misses.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Enabled/total baseline and firmware core-disable policy.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: OS online CPUs include threads and can change independently; correlation requires topology mapping and cannot redefine the SMBIOS field.

project_override_considerations: A project may approve disabled or fused-off physical cores by socket, but must state the exact enabled count and cannot substitute logical CPU or online-mask counts.
expected_evidence: Approved enabled/total core matrix, BIOS/fuse policy, decode rule and tool versions
Complete pre-reboot Type 4 table with socket/status, formatted length, raw legacy/extended fields and effective enabled count
Consistency result against total cores and optional layer-aware OS topology evidence
Approved reboot/health evidence and equivalent post-reboot comparison
Engineer verdict with any authorized disabled/fused-core rationale

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The item and criterion consistently target Enabled Core Count; firmware policy and expected values are project inputs.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The fields are safely readable and their relationships are defined once project policy is provided.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Adds raw legacy/extended encoding, socket mapping and consistency with total cores.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Retains useful BIOS/OS topology context while correcting capability to FULLY AUTOMATABLE and separating verdict ownership.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.v3_1_improvement: Explicitly separates firmware-enabled physical cores from OS online logical CPUs and covers Enabled Core Count 2.

review_improvement: Prevents a plausible displayed value from concealing truncation, an impossible enabled-greater-than-total relationship or layer-confused OS comparison.
independent_technical_reasoning: With approved enabled-core policy, all core extraction, effective-value calculation, consistency checks and reboot comparison are software-controlled.
